text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed slightly down on low volume on Tuesday, reconfirming the market's depression due to investor concern over slow economic growth, brokers said.
The outlook until next year was more of the same, they added.

"We've got this (trend) at least until the end of the year," said Luis Calderon of the local brokerage Acciones y Valores. "We are not hitting the growth targets agreed with the International Monetary Fund. If we do not meet the goals, we lose credibility in the eyes of the investors."
The General Index fell 1.10 percent to 1,443.9 points and the blue-chip Selective Index fell 0.69 percent to 2,017.8 points, according to preliminary stock figures.

This year's rise in gross domestic product should not only be well down on the government's original six percent growth estimate, but will also likely be below the bottom-end goal of three percent agreed with the IMF mid-way in May.
The government announced earlier this month that the economy grew 1.9 percent in the first nine months of the year, compared with 8.9 percent in the same period of 1995.
Monday, benchmark Telefonica del Peru bucked the downward trend, closing up 0.19 percent at 5.24 soles, in low volume of 285,000 shares, according to preliminary figures.
Electricity distributor Luz del Sur, which saw the sale of the state's 30 percent stake in the company start on Monday, dropped 3.46 percent to 3.35 soles on volume of 135,000 shares.
In a total of 1,189 trades, volume was estimated at 26.0 million soles ($10.1 million)
